status.en: 170 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 26% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 170 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 26 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen continue abducting civilians and attacking security forces across northern Nigeria, with recent incidents including the kidnapping of a university student in Plateau, the abduction of two visually impaired persons in Plateau, and the seizure of 14 schoolchildren from a farm. Security operatives have rescued multiple victims, such as eight abducted residents in Kaduna, a pregnant woman and seven others in Kaduna, and a group of 37 worshippers held for 212 days in Kaduna. Bandits have killed vigilantes, including a 18‑year-old in Plateau and a young woman in Bauchi, and police officers in a Sokoto-Zamfara highway ambush. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn fortsetter å bortføre sivile og angripe sikkerhetsstyrker over hele Nord-Nigeria, med nylige hendelser som kidnapping av en universitetsstudent i Plateau, bortføring av to synshemmede personer i Plateau, og beslagleggelse av 14 skolebarn fra en gård. Sikkerhetsoperatører har reddet flere ofre, som åtte bortførte innbyggere i Kaduna, en gravid kvinne og syv andre i Kaduna, og en gruppe på 37 tilbedere holdt i 212 dager i Kaduna. Banditter har drept vigilante, inkludert en 18‑åring i Plateau og en ung kvinne i Bauchi, samt politifolk i et bakholdsangrep på motorveien mellom Sokoto og Zamfara. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
